references.text: Earlier that same day, Jesus had begun to explain the Scriptures to the travelers on the road to Emmaus: [ref:Luk 24:27|Luke 24:27]. Now he opens all the disciples' minds to understand the same thing.
The travelers from Emmaus described how their hearts burned as Jesus opened the Scriptures for them ([ref:Luk 24:32|Luke 24:32]). Verse 45 describes this same action extended to all the disciples.
The Lord opened Lydia's heart to pay attention to what Paul said ([ref:Apg 16:14|Acts 16:14]). The same Greek word (διανοίγω) is used for God opening the mind or heart to understand his word.

Paul opened (διανοίγω) the Scriptures for them in Thessalonica and explained that the Messiah had to suffer and rise ([ref:Apg 17:2-3|Acts 17:2-3]). This exactly reflects what Jesus did for the disciples in Luke 24:45.

The psalmist prays: "Open my eyes, so that I may behold wondrous things out of your law" ([ref:Sal 119:18|Psalm 119:18]). This expresses the same spiritual truth that God must open a person's understanding to comprehend Scripture.
"Give me understanding, so that I may learn your commandments" ([ref:Sal 119:73|Psalm 119:73]). The prayer for divine understanding to grasp God's word parallels what Jesus does in Luke 24:45.

Paul writes that a veil lies over the minds of the Israelites when they read the old covenant, but it is removed in Christ ([ref:2 Kor 3:14-16|2 Corinthians 3:14-16]). This is theologically parallel: without Christ's revelation, the meaning of Scripture remains hidden.

Paul prays that "the eyes of your heart may be enlightened" for believers ([ref:Ef 1:18|Ephesians 1:18]). This prayer reflects the same need for divine illumination that Jesus gave to the disciples in Luke 24:45.

The preceding verse ([ref:Luk 24:44|Luke 24:44]) shows that Jesus pointed out that everything written about him in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms had to be fulfilled. Verse 45 is the concrete action where he opens their minds to understand this.

The following verses ([ref:Luk 24:46-47|Luke 24:46-47]) show the content of what the disciples now understood: that the Messiah would suffer, rise, and that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed to all nations.

Paul teaches that God's Spirit reveals what God has prepared, and that we have received the Spirit to understand what God in his grace has given us ([ref:1 Kor 2:10-12|1 Corinthians 2:10-12]). This is the same principle of divine illumination for understanding Scripture.
